hints: Focus on what straight-chain means here, a continuous C-C-C-C backbone with no branches, so you only vary where the two Cl atoms go.
Fix the first Cl at C1 and then move the second Cl from C1 to C2 to C3 to C4 to list the 1,x family, then do the same starting at C2.
Remember structural isomerism only counts different connectivity, so do not split the same connectivity into optical or cis-trans forms and do not double count symmetric pairs like 1,4 and 4,1.
walkthrough:
**Fix the carbon skeleton**

Great start, straight-chain means the carbon backbone is always the same.

$$ \text{C - C - C - C} $$
So every isomer is just a dichlorobutane, we only decide the two positions for Cl on carbons 1 to 4.

**List isomers with a Cl on C1**

Keep one Cl on carbon 1 and walk the second Cl along the chain.

$$ 1,1: \text{CHCl}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 $$
$$ 1,2: \text{CH}_2\text{ClCHClCH}_2\text{CH}_3 $$
$$ 1,3: \text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{CHClCH}_3 $$
$$ 1,4: \text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} $$
That gives 4 distinct connectivities.

**List isomers with no Cl on C1**

Now start at C2. The only new possibilities are both Cls in the middle.

$$ 2,2: \text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 $$
$$ 2,3: \text{CH}_3\text{CHClCHClCH}_3 $$
Anything like 3,3 is the same as 2,2, and 3,4 is the same as 1,2, just numbered from the other end, so we stop.

**Add them up, ignoring stereoisomerism**

We have 4 + 2 = 6 structural isomers.

The 2,3-isomer can exist as meso and optical forms and 1,2- and 1,3- can have chiral centres, but the question says structural only, so each connectivity counts once.

options.A: Correct. There are 6 straight-chain structural isomers: 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3-, 1,4-, 2,2- and 2,3-dichlorobutane. No branched skeletons are allowed and stereoisomers are not counted separately.
options.B: Incorrect. 7 usually comes from accidentally counting one stereoisomer extra, most often splitting 2,3-dichlorobutane into meso and racemic forms. The question asks for structural isomerism only, so 2,3 counts as one.
options.C: Incorrect. 8 often comes from counting stereoisomers for both 1,2- and 2,3- or from including a branched skeleton like 1,2-dichloro-2-methylpropane. Only the straight C4 chain is allowed here.
options.D: Incorrect. 9 is too high and usually comes from counting all stereoisomers plus double counting symmetric pairs such as counting 1,4 and 4,1 or 1,3 and 3,1 as different. Numbering from either end gives the same structural isomer.
